solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Dry and stony hill area

parts.note: sec is the French-derived word for dry, used of wine
a tor is a rocky hilltop, as on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: A description of barren, rocky upland terrain.
explanation.walkthrough: TOR is a craggy hill, common in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: A sector is a distinct part or zone, a synonym for an area.

clue.text: Possibly sigh about unusual din coming from a party

indicators.note: about says the first piece goes round the second
possibly says sigh may be another arrangement of its letters
unusual says the letters of din take an odd order

explanation.surface: Someone sighs at the strange racket from a party next door.
explanation.walkthrough: SHIG (from 'sigh', by 'Possibly') goes 'about' IND (from 'din', by 'unusual'); 'coming from a' is link.
explanation.definitionFit: A noisy, lively celebration is a party, the informal sense of the word.

clue.text: Match later restaged in the centre

indicators.note: in means one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: the core is the centre of something

indicators.note: restaged says the word later is put on again in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A sports fixture is replayed later at the central ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'restaged' makes RELAT from LATER, placed 'in' CORE.
explanation.definitionFit: To correspond or tally is to match, a verb sense of linking two things systematically.

clue.text: Love to head the fight-back by word of mouth

indicators.note: to head means the first piece sits on top of the second in this down entry

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, the letter O
a rally is a recovery or comeback

explanation.surface: Someone's affection leads a comeback, all told in conversation.
explanation.definitionFit: Spoken rather than written communication is delivered by mouth, the adverb sense.

clue.text: For pain alleviation it's outstanding

definitions.meaning: to bring relief from pain, as a remedy is taken
standing out from the surface, as carving does

explanation.surface: A remedy is praised as excellent at easing pain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outstanding' looks like praise but means literally projecting, as a carved design raised from its background.
explanation.definitionFit: Raised carving is said to be done in relief; and a pill taken to ease suffering is for relief.

clue.text: Ones for reform — yet they vote against

indicators.note: for reform says the letters of ones are re-formed into another order

explanation.surface: Those calling for reform still oppose it in the vote.
explanation.walkthrough: 'yet' is link.
explanation.definitionFit: In Parliament the voters against a motion are counted as the No side, plural.

clue.text: Balanced prepared diet rounds off the day

parts.note: even means level or balanced

indicators.note: prepared says diet is made up into another arrangement

explanation.surface: A sensible meal ends a person's day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'prepared' makes TIDE from DIET.
explanation.definitionFit: The poetic word for evening, the time that ends the daylight hours.

clue.text: Urge on the politician that is left outside

indicators.note: outside says the letters for that is wrap round the politician

parts.note: i.e. abbreviates id est, that is
MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A politician is excluded and pushed to act.
explanation.definitionFit: To drive or press someone forward is to spur or push them, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Intended to include new money

indicators.note: to include means the first piece goes round the second

parts.note: one's intended is the person one is engaged to

explanation.surface: Someone planned to bring in fresh cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Intended' is a noun here, a betrothed partner, not 'meant'.
explanation.definitionFit: Funds or capital for a venture, the noun sense of money.

clue.text: Attack as unsafe place for children to play

definitions.meaning: an advance or incursion into enemy territory

definitions.text: unsafe place for children to play
definitions.meaning: on the street among traffic, read as two words

explanation.surface: A warning about the danger of children playing amid traffic.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer 2,4 for the second sense: children playing amid traffic.
explanation.definitionFit: An incursion or advance into hostile ground is a raid made on it, so an attack.

clue.text: Safe to criticise one who never grew up

parts.note: peter is old criminal slang for a safe
to pan is to review harshly

explanation.surface: Someone decides it is safe to knock a childish adult.
explanation.walkthrough: PETER as a safe is thieves' slang (a safe-cracker is a peterman).
explanation.definitionFit: J. M. Barrie's character is the boy who refused to grow older, living in Neverland.

clue.text: Crafty ruse he'd introduced

indicators.note: crafty suggests the letters are cunningly reworked

explanation.surface: A man brought in a cunning trick.
explanation.definitionFit: To show a guest in or bring something in is to present or lead it in, as an attendant does.

clue.text: Second employer

parts.note: a second is the assistant in a duel, engaged by the person fighting it

explanation.surface: Reads like someone's next job after the first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second' is not an ordinal but the attendant who supports a combatant in a duel.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone fighting a formal pistol or sword contest appoints a second as an aide, so in effect employs one.

clue.text: European leader made his mark when about fifty

indicators.note: about means the first piece goes round the second

parts.note: to stain is to leave a mark
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A statesman left his imprint on history around the half-century.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: The Soviet dictator was head of the USSR, a European power, for decades.

clue.text: Unusually long creeper seen round Italian city

indicators.note: seen round says the first piece wraps the second

parts.note: a boa is a snake, a creeping creature

indicators.note: unusually says the letters of long take an odd order

explanation.surface: A huge climbing plant is spotted around an Italian town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'creeper' suggests a plant but is the snake; 'Unusually' makes LOGN from LONG.
explanation.definitionFit: The capital of Emilia-Romagna in northern Italy, famous for its university.

clue.text: Bag snatch

definitions.meaning: to bag is to seize or claim something
to snatch is to take hold quickly

explanation.surface: A bag-snatching, a street theft.
explanation.definitionFit: To bag or snatch something is to seize it eagerly, a verb sense meaning take hold of.

clue.text: Naval officer back with wife?

parts.note: to second a motion is to back it
a mate is a spouse or partner

explanation.surface: A sailor returns home with his wife.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' is a verb, support, not returning.
explanation.definitionFit: On a ship the officer ranking below the first mate holds this rank; strictly merchant navy, loosely naval.

clue.text: Like some stories, can lead to novel

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters take a new order

explanation.surface: Tales can give rise to a book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' looks like a book but is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Tales told from hearsay and personal accounts are informal and unverified, the adjective.

clue.text: Stop one on a horse

parts.note: to stall is to stop running
I is the Roman numeral for one
taken as written

explanation.surface: An instruction to halt someone riding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a' is link.
explanation.definitionFit: An uncastrated male horse, used for breeding, is an example.

clue.text: Into action without restraint

definitions.meaning: First World War soldiers went out of the trenches into battle this way

explanation.surface: Charging into battle recklessly.
explanation.definitionFit: Soldiers leaving trenches climbed the parapet into combat; the idiom now also describes something excessive or exaggerated.

clue.text: He didn't trust his wife to look after a new hotel

indicators.note: after puts the look piece behind the shuffled one
new says the letters of hotel form a fresh arrangement

parts.note: lo is an old word for look

explanation.surface: A suspicious husband runs a hotel, leaving his wife to manage it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'look after' reads as care for, but splits: 'new' shuffles the hotel, and 'after' places the old word for look behind it.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's Moor is goaded by Iago into jealously doubting Desdemona's fidelity.

clue.text: She's over acting in part

indicators.note: in part says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An actress is accused of hamming it up.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took "She's" as the definition, but a name cannot stand for 'she is'; the definition is 'She', and the 's is the link 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's given name, so an example of a she.

clue.text: Guardian supported by American in daily prayers

indicators.note: supported by puts the first piece above the second in this down entry

parts.note: a guardian angel watches over someone
US abbreviates United States, American

explanation.surface: A protector backed by an American figure in morning devotions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is link.
explanation.definitionFit: The Catholic devotion recited morning, noon and evening commemorating the Incarnation, a set of prayers.

clue.text: Humble cleric taking me to heart

indicators.note: taking means the first piece holds the second
to heart says the second piece goes into the middle

parts.note: a dean is a senior cleric

explanation.surface: A modest churchman embraces me.
explanation.definitionFit: To humble or degrade someone is to lower them in dignity, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Old crone gets leg broken into the bargain

parts.note: a hag is an ugly old woman

indicators.note: broken says the letters of leg are rearranged

explanation.surface: An old woman fractures a leg, and that's not all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'into the bargain' looks like 'besides', but 'bargain' is a verb here; 'broken' makes GLE from LEG.
explanation.definitionFit: To bargain is to dispute over a price, the same as to haggle in a market.

clue.text: Serious, but not acute

definitions.meaning: the accent sloping the other way from the acute accent

explanation.surface: A medical condition is serious though not sudden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'acute' suggests a sharp illness; here it is the accent mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Solemn or weighty matters are serious; the accent ` opposite to ´ is named likewise.

clue.text: Being grounded, perhaps, and made a scapegoat

definitions.note: loosely, someone put upon and expected to lose; the clue phrase stands for the person it happens to

indicators.note: perhaps says the letters of grounded might be arranged another way

explanation.surface: A teenager is kept at home as punishment and wrongly blamed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grounded' suggests a teenager's punishment but is the fodder; 'perhaps' shuffles it. 'Being' and 'and' are link words. The definition is loose: a scapegoat and the expected loser are not quite the same.
explanation.definitionFit: The disadvantaged party, put upon and expected to lose, is the one given a raw deal, as a scapegoat is.

clue.text: Gets older and agrees about being dropped

indicators.note: being dropped says those letters are removed from agrees

parts.note: re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: Someone gets older and goes along with being cut from the team.
explanation.definitionFit: Growing older is a verb sense, someone matures or advances in years.

clue.text: Crumbs! Svengali's gone mad!

indicators.note: something gone mad is wildly disordered, so the name's letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: An exclamation of surprise that the sinister hypnotist has lost his mind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crumbs!' looks like an exclamation but is the definition; Svengali is the hypnotist in du Maurier's Trilby.
explanation.definitionFit: Leftover bits of food after a meal, such as crumbs, are scraps or remains.

clue.text: Crazy lament?

indicators.note: crazy says the letters of lament are put in a wild new order

explanation.surface: Asks whether a dirge is unhinged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crazy' does double duty: the anagram signal and the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Mad or unhinged, a colloquial sense of mentally disturbed.

clue.text: Quality of unconcealed hospitality

definitions.meaning: the state of being open or not hidden
a generous, welcoming manner towards guests

explanation.surface: A frank and generous welcome to guests.
explanation.definitionFit: Frankness and a lack of concealment is candour; welcoming guests with open arms and an open house is generosity.

clue.text: They are all right in the square

definitions.text: They are all right in the square

parts.words: They are all right in the square
parts.note: each corner of a square measures ninety degrees

explanation.surface: People in a town square are said to be fine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'all right' sounds like 'fine' but means every one is a right one, of ninety degrees.
explanation.definitionFit: A square's four corners are each ninety degrees, so all of them are of the right kind.
